text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Purpura Fulminans secondary to neonatal sepsis. The combination of a non-blanching, purpuric rash, maternal antibiotic exposure history (often for Group B Strep prophylaxis), and the urgent need for coagulation studies strongly suggests disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) triggered by an occult bacterial infection. Immediate broad-spectrum antibiotics and supportive care are required.
